themes.consensus_view: Banks are split on whether the AI complex is a bubble: Bank of America and The Market Ear point to dotcom-era swings in single stocks and unsustainable borrowing to fund AI, while UBS and Goldman read the recent drop as investors trimming crowded positions rather than a break in the underlying earnings story.

facts_agreed.claim: AI infrastructure is the dominant driver of current S&P 500 earnings growth.
evidence_quotes: AI infrastructure = ~60% of S&P 500 EPS growth this quarter.

facts_contested.claim: whether the AI/hyperscaler complex is a bubble
facts_contested.for_evidence: single stock realized vol has risen to levels last seen in the late 90s dotcom bubble
facts_contested.against_evidence: sell-off in AI capex and other crowded winners looks increasingly like a technical de-grossing event

themes.consensus_view: Five desks reference disruption to the Strait of Hormuz oil chokepoint as a live macro risk, but none has staked out a directional price call on it yet.

facts_agreed.claim: Five banks flag Strait of Hormuz supply and shipping disruption as an active Middle East risk this window.
evidence_quotes: Strait of Hormuz energy flow disruptions

themes.consensus_view: Three research desks flag a hawkish turn in Federal Reserve policy (the Fed leaning toward keeping interest rates high rather than cutting) as a live backdrop, but none has staked out a clear directional call on it.

facts_agreed.claim: Three banks reference a hawkish shift in Fed policy as a current market backdrop without arguing a directional view.

themes.consensus_view: Both banks agree everyday retail investors have become a major, active force in the market, with Goldman treating them as core price-setters while Vanda notes they are picking specific high-conviction stocks rather than buying the whole market.

facts_agreed.claim: Retail investors have become an increasingly influential and active force in the current market.
evidence_quotes: retail aren't buying the broad market. They're buying the stories they have the highest conviction in.
retail is becoming an integral part of the eco system

themes.consensus_view: Both Bank of America desks think gold's pullback from its highs is not finished yet, arguing it has been too brief and too shallow to fully play out, with a bearish chart signal pointing to more downside.

facts_agreed.claim: The gold correction is not yet complete and likely has more time and downside to run.
evidence_quotes: the YTD correction requires more time and potentially more depth to complete
The current correction is only 24 weeks old versus the prior 121-week advance.
